fields.description:
## Problem
The reconciler multi-project fan-out (story 1734) runs every mapped project's base
(active + done-recent) JQL queries in a single flat loop with NO per-project error
isolation: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` builds
`queries` across all projects and iterates `for jql, cap in queries:` — any single
project's transport failure (ACLI 400 unknown-project, 401/403 permission, 404,
429 rate-limit, 5xx, timeout) propagates out and ABORTS THE ENTIRE PASS for all
projects. The enrichment loop directly below already fails open per-project
(`_enrich_project` "each pass failing open independently so a per-project fault
degrades only that project"). The base-query loop never inherited that resilience.

This is the PROVEN root cause of the 2026-08-15 production outage (bug
05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27): a single mapped-but-nonexistent project key (`LEG`) —
syntactically valid, so `_validate_project_key` passes — made ACLI exit 1 and took
down ~12h of scheduled Reconcile Bridge passes across every project.

## Approach
Extract a `_fetch_project(client, proj, pass_id, repo_root, alert_store)` helper
(symmetric to `_enrich_project`) that drains BOTH base queries (active +
done-recent) for one project into a LOCAL dict and returns it. `_build_snapshot`
calls it inside a per-project try/except and merges the returned dict into the
shared `snapshot`/`seen_keys` ONLY on success. This makes the no-partial-merge
contract true by construction: a transport failure mid-pagination of the active
query, or after the active query merged but the done-recent query fails, discards
that project's LOCAL dict entirely — no partial keys ever reach the shared snapshot
where the differ would read them as deletions.

On a per-project transport error the boundary emits an observable alert via
`alert_store.append({"kind": "fetcher-project-fetch-failed", "project": <key>,
"pass_id": pass_id, ...})`, discards the local dict, and CONTINUEs to the other
projects. Preserve the existing fail-CLOSED behavior for a
syntactically-invalid/absent key: `jql_active`/`jql_done_recent` call
`_validate_project_key` OUTSIDE the per-project try (bug 626d intent unchanged) so a
bad key still aborts the pass. Preserve the re-raise of `BackendPaginationStallError`
(a stalled pager is a truncated whole-project read and must still surface),
matching the enrichment loop's exception handling exactly. Keep the dedup
(`seen_keys`) and the `fetcher-dedup-suppressed` alert behavior intact — dedup now
runs at the atomic merge of each project's local dict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One mapped project's base-query transport error does not abort the pass; the other projects' issues still land in the snapshot, and NO partial keys from the failed project are merged. Verified by the new unit `test_one_project_base_query_failure_does_not_abort_pass` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py`.
- [x] A per-project base-query fetch failure emits an observable `fetcher-project-fetch-failed` alert naming the project and pass_id. Verified: the new unit asserts a matching record in `bridge_state/bridge_alerts/*.jsonl`.
- [x] The single-project (unseeded store) path remains regression-identical. Verified: the existing `test_single_project_fallback_is_regression_identical` still passes.
- [x] A syntactically-invalid/absent key still fails closed (626d preserved) and a `BackendPaginationStallError` still re-raises. Verified: `_validate_project_key` is still called by `jql_active`/`jql_done_recent` outside the per-project try, and the boundary re-raises `BackendPaginationStallError` exactly as `_enrich_project` does.

## Testing
Add an always-on unit (no live Jira) to `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py`
using a `_FakeClient` whose `search_issues` RAISES for project `BAD` (e.g. an
`HTTPError`/ACLI error) but returns issues for `OK`; assert `OK`'s issues land in
the snapshot, the pass is not aborted, and the `fetcher-project-fetch-failed` alert
fired for `BAD`. This is the always-on regression the incident lacked (closes the
P0-3 test gap). Mutation check: reverting the per-project try/except returns the
test to RED. Run with
`python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py -q`,
plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Sequencing
Edits `fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` base-query region. Ticket C (non-Done status)
also edits `fetcher.py` — C is sequenced AFTER this ticket to avoid conflict.
